subject: qilin
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: qilin, scaled hooved chimera with antlers and cloud mane.
Style: high-fantasy anime.
reasoning:
I'm planning the qilin design as a chimera with dragon head, deer body, ox tail, scaled hide, and hooves, aiming for a high-fantasy anime look using cel shading, glowing anime eyes, and ink-style fur edges from the toon kit.

Now I'm sketching the skeleton: hips as root around hip height 1.0m, a spine chain running from rump to chest, a neck chain into head and jaw, four legs with IK, and a tail chain, with the body around 1.4m at the shoulder and total height near 2.2m including antlers. I'm laying out the body as a sweep along the spine path from rump (z=-0.5) to chest (z=0.45), with back height ~1.15 and belly ~0.75, and starting to define the hips joint as the root/first spine joint in the builder.

I'm shaping a dragon-like head angled forward with a boxy snout and jaw, lowering the neck end to about 1.6m for proportion. For the tail, I'm chaining it backward from the hips with a drooping ox-tail curve ending in a flame-tuft tip, then starting to loft the torso body between the hips and spine joints with stations along that path.

Now I'm working out the exact width and height values at each station along the spine, trying to get the back higher than the belly for a natural qilin profile, while checking whether the loft path needs to align precisely with the joint positions in the bone chain.

I'll build the spine path using the same points as the loft centers for consistency, then figure out where to place loft stations relative to the chain's start and end so extra tail and rump points fall outside the chain and get assigned correctly. For the neck, I'm setting up a sweep with tapering radii along the neck chain, accounting for overlap where it meets the body.

For colors, I'm settling on a high-fantasy palette: deep teal-jade scales with cream-gold belly, golden hooves, and a mane that reads as fire shifting from crimson to gold. I'm picturing the antlers in gold and coral with glowing tips, and the mane itself rendered as cloud-like swirling card shapes in pale cyan and white with gold trim.

Writing scale and belly paint definitions...

I'm thinking about adding a lower-leg coloring effect, giving the legs a warmer gold/cream "sock" tone below a certain height with a zigzag fur edge for texture.

Also realizing the shared paint sheet's texel density drops as I add more painted parts, so I need to keep that in mind when deciding how many regions to paint.

I'm sizing the paint resolution: the body's painted area needs roughly 1cm texels at this scale, so a 2048 sheet with a 4096 atlas should be safe, falling back to halving if things don't fit.

Now I'm shifting to building the head itself — dragon-like, mounted at the neck joint and angled slightly forward-down, with the skull, snout, brow ridges, nostrils, and cheeks constructed from basic shapes in the head's local coordinate frame.

I'm adding the remaining head details: whiskers sweeping back, fangs, a separately-jointed jaw with teeth, decal eyes on the skull, fin-shaped ears, branching gold antlers with glowing tines, and a tuft of beard cards under the chin. For the head joint orientation, I'm weighing whether to tilt it slightly downward to match the snout or keep it aimed straight forward and let the neck curve handle the bend — leaning toward the simpler straight-forward option with the neck's tangent absorbing the angle.

I'm defining a helper function that converts left/up/forward offsets into local positions relative to the head joint, then setting the jaw as a child joint of the head for building its own parts.

Now I'm laying out the skull as a sphere, the snout as a tapered frustum box, and adding a small nostril bump near the tip. I'm shaping the lower jaw as another tapered frustum attached to the jaw joint, with cone-shaped teeth placed along the upper and lower jaw edges.

Thinking about overall scale, I want the head somewhat oversized for the anime proportions on a horse-sized body. For the eyes, I'm planning to use a decal technique with an anime-style eye texture placed on the side of the skull, positioning it outward-facing near the front of the head.

I'm working out the dir vector so eyes face slightly forward and up, and sizing the skull as a bulbous ellipsoid centered near the eye region so the surface has room for the decals. I'm considering using an angular helper that locates points on the skull surface by azimuth and elevation, similar to how the kit example places things around a head center.

For the eye color, I'm leaning toward a vivid gold-orange iris against the teal skin for contrast, and planning subtle brow ridges above the eyes in a darker teal or gold tone to add character.

Now I'm figuring out the ears, imagining fin-like dragon ears swept back and outward using an extruded leaf-shaped outline with smoothed edges, angled so they point backward and slightly outward from the head.

Thinking about antlers next — planning to sprout a main beam from a hit point on the skull at a chosen azimuth.

Setting up antler sprout joints...

Adding gold-coral gradient coloring...

I'm now designing the mane as cloud-card textures along the neck, planning ruyi-cloud swirl shapes with white-teal shading and gold outlines, using multiple double-sided cloud variants of different sizes.

I'm placing these cloud cards along the dorsal sweep curve, orienting them to flow backward along the neck, and adding extra tufts at the shoulders, elbows, fetlocks, and tail for a fuller cloud-fur effect.

For the cloud texture itself, I'm sketching a tapered teardrop shape like a stylized "ruyi" curl -- fat at the root, curling to a point at the tip -- with a soft gradient fill transitioning from white to cyan.

Writing SVG swirl strokes...

Now I'm thinking about adding golden flame accents elsewhere on the qilin, maybe wisps near the ankles or a glowing tuft at the tail tip to echo its mythic fire motif.

I also want a row of small golden diamond-shaped plates running along the spine, using a helper to sample points along the body's dorsal sweep curve and placing little gold ridge spikes at each one.

For the flanks, I'll add glowing gold cloud-spiral emblems as decals, like a kirin crest, since glow can apply to decal textures too.

Now for the legs, I'm setting up IK chains for deer/horse-style limbs with hooves — defining shoulder, elbow, knee, fetlock, and hoof joint positions and segment lengths for the forelegs.

I'm reconsidering whether to add a fourth length for the hoof itself, maybe setting target y to around the fetlock height and naming the tip joint accordingly so the hoof geometry sits below it.

For the hoof shape, since this is a qilin with deer-like cloven hooves, I'm planning to build it from two small frustum halves side by side in a gold tone, plus optional dewclaws for extra detail rather than a single plain cone.

Now I'm working through the leg sweeps, tapering radii from the shoulder down to a narrower cannon and fetlock. For the hind legs, I'm figuring out the joint chain—hip, stifle bending forward, hock bending backward, down to a roughly vertical cannon—working out segment lengths and bend directions so the overall leg bends naturally like a horse's hind leg.

Checking the limb reach: the hip-to-hock distance comes out under the sum of segment lengths, so the pose is geometrically feasible. Since I can't actually execute code to verify this, I need to be cautious about the limb API's exact behavior, especially risky parts like the limb function's signature and its optional parameters.

The chain spans joints from shoulder to hoof, with forelegs parenting to the chest joint and hindlegs to the hips, and I'm planning to add rounded muscle shapes at the shoulder/thigh joints blended with body paint, switching to leg paint further down, and cloven hoof shapes at the tips.

Working out the hoof geometry with split frustum halves positioned near the floor, using warm gold tones for the outer and inner hoof surfaces, plus small fetlock tufts and belly placement details.

Now I'm designing the ox tail with a drooping chain path from the hips down to a low tip, scaling the tail's thickness and color along its length, and capping it with a cloud-and-flame tuft ring at the end.

Now I'm shaping that tuft so the cards face outward and droop downward with a leaning bend, adding a glowing flame accent while keeping the cloud cluster. I'm also planning the jaw and head joints, sweeping long flowing gold whiskers from the upper lip outward with small glowing pearl tips, and sketching a goatee of flame-textured cards hanging from the jaw bone.

I'm making sure each card and sweep explicitly specifies its bone (head or jaw) rather than relying on nearest-joint inference, then adding a glowing cyan forehead gem between the horns with a gold lozenge backing, and starting to design jagged cheek frills as an extruded fin shape.

For the nostrils and small upper fangs I'm planning dark ellipsoid shapes, and for the body I'm working out a gold swirl emblem decal projected onto the flank surface of the loft, figuring out the right position, direction, and orientation so it reads correctly from outside the model without needing asymmetric mirroring.

I'm also thinking through adding a decorative neck collar made from a closed-loop sweep positioned along the neck joint, with jade pearls and a hanging bell accented by red ribbon streamers, trying to figure out how to anchor the bell at a specific point along that loop.

I'm planning out the remaining textures (flame, emblem, scale runes) and tallying up part counts across antlers, scales, teeth, and mane sections to hit around 200 total parts. Now I'm starting to write the actual import statements and setup code for the build.

Finalizing imports...

I'm sketching out the color palette, defining jade and gold tones with their lighter and darker variants for shading.

Setting up scale and belly paint patterns...

Adjusting the fur edge zigzag direction for the leg...

Now I'm defining the paint layers for the head and snout, using a similar countershaded scale pattern but with a slightly smaller scale size, plus a separate gold paint layer that reuses flat color materials shared across parts.

Writing the cloud swirl SVG texture...

Still writing SVG shapes...

Still writing path coordinates... Now I'm defining a second cloud texture with a pale gold gradient fill and warm brown outline for variety.

I'm also building a flame texture with multiple tongues using a gold-to-red gradient outer path and a yellow-white inner path, meant for beards, tail tips, fetlock flames, and glow effects, plus a gold spiral emblem texture resembling a ruyi cloud swirl.

Writing builder setup code...

I'll skip the sides option and leave it default to avoid type errors, then set up joints for hips, spine, neck, and head using catmull-rom paths with parent relationships chained correctly, making sure positions connect smoothly between segments.

For the jaw, I'm defining a helper that converts local offsets relative to the head joint into world directions for aim and position. Then I'm sketching the body loft stations along the spine path with varying width and height to give it a natural tapered silhouette from front to back.

Now I'm checking that leg placement sits reasonably within the body's cross-section, and working out the neck sweep radii so it tapers smoothly and matches the body's radius where they join.

For the head, I'm sketching the skull as a scaled sphere ellipsoid, then shaping the snout as a tapered frustum box running from the face forward, with widths along X and height along the aim-normal so the box orients correctly. I'm also starting on the upper lip and nose pad geometry to sit over the snout.

Now I'm adding the nose details—nostril spheres, a small gold nose knob spike—then moving to the jaw as its own tapered frustum bone, colored with a cream underside for the belly countershade. I'm placing a dark red interior mouth box and beginning the teeth: upper fangs as downward-pointing cones at the snout, lower fangs pointing upward from the jaw, plus a planned row of smaller teeth along each side.

For the eyes, I'm computing their position by sampling a point on the skull surface at a given azimuth and elevation, sizing them generously for an anime look, and mirroring the decal for the opposite side. I'm considering a subtle glow on the eye decals to give them a shiny look, then starting to think through how to attach brow ridges as a sweep curve sitting on the skull surface.

Now I'm sketching out the ear shape as an extruded outline profile.

Still working through type signatures...

Working out the ear orientation vectors...

Now I'm defining the cheek frill shape as a jagged star-like outline, checking the points go around without self-crossing, and giving it a golden color.

Moving on to the antlers, I'm looping over both sides of the skull to find the root point for each antler, then starting to build out the beam path from that base point.

I'm sketching the control points for each antler beam curving upward and backward from the root, then reconsidering the overall height since 0.6 units above the head makes them too tall -- scaling down toward 0.5 feels more proportional for a qilin-style antler.

Still writing antler sprouting logic...

Simplifying tines to a flat gold color since the toon style relies on scene lighting rather than per-element gradients anyway.

Adding tine glow accents...

Now I'm shaping the antler base with a gold cylinder cup at the root to suggest the burr, then moving on to building mane strands along the dorsal line of the neck using the neck spline's angle frames.

Then I'm setting up the card appearance with lean, flow, bend, and spin parameters to give the mane a windswept, layered look, noting that cards orient along the surface normal at each frame.

I'm adding a small tuft of clouds behind the head near the horns, placing frames around the skull at specific azimuth/elevation ranges, plus a beard element with flame-like cards hanging from the jaw underside, adjusting lean and flow so they drape backward naturally.

Now I'm making the beard a glowing gold flame texture for a fantasy effect, then moving to the neck collar and bell—sweeping a closed loop around the neck bone at a fixed lift to create a gold band, while deciding whether to let the path inherit its own bone weights rather than forcing a single bone.

Adding bell and jade bead details...

Confirming the frame/bone inheritance works since sphere orientation doesn't matter, so `{ at }` is sufficient. Now I'm placing a row of small cone-shaped gold ridge plates along the dorsal line of the body using `b.along`, with each one embedded partially into the surface at its normal direction.

I'll generate the ridge spikes along the body between t=0.1 and 0.85. For shoulder and hip puffs, I'm placing angled cards at the body surface near the shoulder (t=0.55) and haunch (t=0.25), sized small and leaning backward to suggest flame-like tufts, plus a flank drag effect.

I'm sweeping tapered geometry along each leg chain with radii narrowing toward the hoof, then layering on muscle details—an ellipsoid at the shoulder/hip root, a small knee pad sphere, and cloud-tuft card decorations at the elbow joint for a fluffy accent.

Now I'm building the tail chain with a tapering sweep radius, adding a ring of tuft cards at the tail's end that face outward along the tail's tangent direction, with leaning and bending parameters to give it a flowing, flame-like cluster look.

I realize the tail's current length would push it below the floor, so I'm adjusting the tail's path points and tuft size downward in reach so everything stays above y=0, keeping the hooves as the only floor-touching points. Verifying overall proportions—back height, head position, and total body length—to confirm the creature reads as roughly horse-sized, then thinking through optional decorative touches like mane ridges or ribbons on the antlers before tallying up the part counts for body, neck, head, antlers, and mane.

Adjusting the eye angle and snout taper to avoid overlap, narrowing the snout width toward the tip for a more dragon-like muzzle, then widening the nose pad itself before moving on to shaping the jaw geometry.

Working out the jaw dimensions to close neatly against the snout for a slightly open mouth pose, then placing upper and lower teeth spikes based on the bottom edge of the snout and top edge of the jaw.
